title: ALMA resolves molecular clouds in metal-poor Magellanic Bridge A
question: What are the gas and dust properties of Magellanic Bridge A at sub-parsec resolution, and is the 870 um submillimeter excess also present at 1.3 mm?

data.sensitivity: continuum rms 0.17 mJy/beam (natural); CO 22-36 mJy/beam per channel

what.value: CO(3-2) peak intensity 0.93+-0.07 K km/s for LABOCA line correction
Dust emissivity per H atom eps_d(345GHz)=3.94e-27 cm2
NANTEN CO(1-0) luminosity 70+-8 K km/s pc2

evidence.quote: We use the 870 $\mu m$ continuum image of Magellanic Bridge A presented in (cite: verdugo2012).

recipe.goal: Reprocess and combine ALMA 12m and 7m data
recipe.method: Archive scripts to calibrate, statwt weights, concat

recipe.goal: Image 1.3 mm continuum and CO(2-1) cube; feather with APEX
recipe.method: clean with natural weighting/taper for continuum, briggs 0.5 for CO; feather with APEX CO

recipe.goal: Aperture photometry for SED and 1.3 mm upper limit
recipe.method: Convolve to common resolution (43'' or 22''), aperture r=50'' or 11'' with sky annulus; upper limit = 3x photometric error
Halpha-based free-free formula (Hunt 2004); CO(3-2) via Drabek 2012

recipe.goal: Fit modified blackbody SED and compute excess and gas mass
recipe.method: Single-component optically thin MBB, chi2 minimisation; excess = measured/predicted flux; gas mass from predicted 870 um flux
key_parameters: beta fixed to 1.4 for North and South
assumptions: distance 60 kpc; dust-to-gas 1/6 solar; kappa_345GHz=1.26; mu=1.36

recipe.goal: Identify CO clouds, fit spectra, derive sizes, luminosities, virial masses, alpha_CO
recipe.method: 3 sigma sources in integrated intensity (172-176 km/s), second moments, Gaussian least-squares to spectra, Rosolowsky & Leroy deconvolution, Mvir=190 R dv^2, alpha_CO=Mvir/L
key_parameters: L_CO=611.5 S dv D^2; R=1.91 sigma_r D
assumptions: spherical bound clouds with rho~r^-1; r21~1; D~60 kpc

evidence.quote: gives a dust temperature $T_d=22.4\pm3.4$ K and an emissivity index $\beta=1.4\pm0.5$

answer_key.quantity: 1.3 mm flux upper limit, Bridge A

evidence.quote: which gives a 1.3 mm flux upper limit for Magellanic Bridge A of 16.5 mJy
The virial mass for CO source North is $437.3\pm26.1$ M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ and for source South is $732.9\pm37.0$ M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$.
$L_{CO(2-1)}= 67.5 \pm 6.3$ K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$ for CO cloud North
$1.29\pm0.07$ pc for cloud North and $1.04\pm0.04$ pc for cloud South

not_stated_but_needed: CO(2-1) cube clean threshold, niter, cell and image size
line-free channels used for the continuum
feather scaling/ single-dish calibration details and Jy/K conversion
how the CO mask from APEX was built
aperture photometry code and SED fit starting values
APEX CO map size is printed in arcsec (likely arcmin), unclear

score_reason: Public ALMA data and clear analysis formulae, but imaging parameters and APEX data processing are partly unspecified.
rediscovery_reason: ALMA data public, recipe largely given, results numeric (virial masses, alpha_CO, upper limits).
